_what: The villa's settings, written down ONCE (architecture review round 17, 2026-11-03): the settings every tablet shares (device-config.json) that hold one value each. The Kiosk's app builds from each row its default (AppConfig DEFAULT_CONFIG), how it reads the villa's copy and its empty (deviceConfig SHARED_KEYS) and the name a change from another tablet is told by (configSlice SETTING_NAMES): src/config/villaSettings.ts. The add-on's server (rootfs/usr/bin/supervisor-proxy.py) reads its defaults and bounds here instead of copies. Before, one setting was written in eight places, and a bound copied into the server could drift from the app's. `kind`: number (any finite number), int (a whole number from `min` to `max`; a number out of range is kept at the nearest bound, a fraction as its whole part), text, entity (an entity id as agent-contract.json `entityPattern` names one, or "" for none), switch (true or false), record (an object, read over `default`). A value of another kind is not kept: the setting reads its default. The app (src/config/villaSettings.ts keptVillaValue) and the server (supervisor-proxy.py _villa_keep, on every save) keep a value by the same rule (owner approved, 2026-11-20). `name`: what the setting's control is called on screen. tests/oracles/shared_config_keys.mjs and tests/store-doors.py read it.
_fullScreenSeconds: How long a full-screen announcement holds the screen (device-config.json `fullScreen`: [{title, seconds}]): whole seconds from `min` to `max`; `default` is a newly picked one's, and the time an older Kiosk's one time for all is read as when it was not one the field took. An item with another time is left out, by the app and the server alike.
_lists: The villa's lists of devices (device-config.json: dismissed, asleep by design): entity ids (agent-contract.json `entityPattern`), each once, in their order; anything else is left out, by the app (deviceConfig idList) and the server alike.
_retired: Keys an older Kiosk stored in the villa's settings and nothing reads any more: the server drops them when it reads the file and from every write (an older tablet's cached page may still send them), once their value is read into today's shape. `alertThresholds`: per-sensor limits no screen ever set (2.496.450). `fullScreenFor`, `ringShownForS`: the picked titles and one time for all, read as `fullScreen` (2.496.670). The Kiosk's own table of migrations (src/config/migrations.ts) retires the same keys from a tablet's own copy.
_examples: The villa's settings as stored or sent (`stored`) and as kept, in today's shape (`today`): the server writes `today` back once and keeps every save so, and the app reads a tablet's own stored copy the same way. Both drive their migration through every one (tests/store-doors.py, tests/oracles/messages_settings.mjs).

examples._: an older Kiosk's titles and one time for all: each title with that time
a time the field never took (or none): the default
no time at all: the default
today's shape beside the retired keys: today's is read, the retired dropped
an item whose time is out of range, or a title twice: left out
a retired key with nothing to read into: dropped
days past the range: kept at the most the field allows
days below the range: kept at the least (0, for ever)
a fraction of a day: its whole days
a value of another kind: not kept, each setting reads its default
a presence sensor that is no entity id: none picked
a list of devices: entity ids, each once, in their order; no list: not kept
each chat's language: a notify entity and a language the agreement names, nothing else
